disclaimer: PROTOTYPE-GRADE DATA. Compiled from public payroll/labor-law summaries and state labor department pages. Rule encodings are conservative simplifications and must be verified by an employment lawyer before production use. Nothing here is legal advice.

rule_kinds.calendar_days: N calendar days after the last day worked.
rule_kinds.immediate: Due on the last day of work (termination day).
rule_kinds.next_payday: The employer's next regular payday. Requires the case's next_payday date.
rule_kinds.none: No state-law deadline for this scenario.
rule_kinds.working_days: N working days (Mon-Fri, holidays not excluded in this prototype) after the last day worked.

states.name: Alabama
states.notes: No Alabama statute sets a final-pay deadline; no federal deadline exists either. Consult an employment lawyer.

states.name: Alaska
states.notes: Quit: next payday at least 3 working days after the last day. Encoded as next_payday with the 3-day minimum noted.

states.name: Arizona
states.notes: Discharge: 7 working days or next regular payday, whichever is earlier.

states.name: Arkansas
states.notes: On employee demand after discharge, payment is due within 7 days of payday; the double-wage penalty anchors to that window.
states.penalty_note: Employer owes DOUBLE the wages due if not paid within 7 days of the payday.

states.name: California
states.notes: Quit with 72+ hours notice: due immediately; without notice: within 72 hours. Encoded conservatively as 72 hours. Exceptions exist for seasonal employees in certain industries.
states.penalty_note: Waiting-time penalties: up to 30 days of the employee's daily wages for willful failure to pay on time (Lab. Code § 203).

states.name: Colorado
states.notes: Immediate upon involuntary separation, with some industry exceptions.

states.name: Connecticut
states.notes: Discharge: next business day.

states.name: District of Columbia
states.notes: Discharge: next working day. Quit: next payday or within 7 days of resignation, whichever is earlier.

states.name: Delaware
states.notes: Sources disagree (next payday vs. later of next payday / 3 days after last day). Encoded conservatively as the LATER of the two to avoid premature demand letters. FLAG: verify with Delaware DOL.

states.name: Florida
states.notes: No Florida final-paycheck statute. Consult an employment lawyer.

states.name: Georgia
states.notes: No Georgia final-paycheck statute. Consult an employment lawyer.

states.name: Hawaii
states.notes: Discharge: immediately, or next working day if same-day payment is impossible. Quit: next payday, or immediately if employee gave at least one pay period's notice.

states.name: Idaho
states.notes: Whichever is earlier: next payday or 10 business days. Written employee request can trigger a 48-hour deadline (excluding weekends/holidays) — not modeled; flag for lawyer review.

states.name: Illinois
states.notes: 'Immediately if possible, but if not, next payday.' Statute sets next regular payday as the hard deadline; encoded as next_payday.

states.name: Indiana
states.notes: Next payday; industry exceptions may apply.

states.name: Kentucky
states.notes: Next payday or 14 days, whichever is later.

states.name: Louisiana
states.notes: Next payday or 15 days after discharge, whichever is earlier.

states.name: Massachusetts
states.notes: Discharge: day of discharge, with limited exceptions.

states.name: Michigan
states.notes: Exceptions for certain industries.

states.name: Minnesota
states.notes: Discharge: within 24 hours of a WRITTEN DEMAND. This prototype uses the last day worked as a proxy for the demand date — FLAG: add a demand-date field before production. Quit: next payday, but no earlier than 5 days and no later than 20 days after the last day.

states.name: Mississippi
states.notes: No Mississippi final-paycheck statute. Consult an employment lawyer.

states.name: Missouri
states.notes: No statute deadline for voluntary quits.

states.name: Montana
states.notes: Discharge: within 4 hours or end of the business day, whichever is first. Quit: next payday or 15 days, whichever is earlier.

states.name: Nebraska
states.notes: Next payday or within 2 weeks, whichever is earlier.

states.name: Nevada
states.notes: Discharge: within 3 days. Quit: next payday or within 7 days, whichever is earlier.

states.name: New Hampshire
states.notes: Discharge: within 72 hours.

states.name: New Mexico
states.notes: Within 5 days; task, piece, and commission wages due within 10 days — wage-type distinction not modeled; FLAG for lawyer review.

states.name: New York
states.notes: Not later than the regular payday for the pay period during which termination occurred.

states.name: Ohio
states.notes: Next payday or within 15 days, whichever is earlier.

states.name: Oregon
states.notes: Discharge: next business day. Quit: on the last day if 48 hours notice was given; otherwise within 5 working days or next payday, whichever is first. Encoded conservatively as 5 working days; intake does not capture notice. FLAG: verify.

states.name: South Carolina
states.notes: Within 48 hours or next payday, not exceeding 30 days.

states.name: Tennessee
states.notes: Next payday or within 21 days, whichever is later.

states.name: Texas
states.notes: Discharge: within 6 calendar days. Quit: next payday.

states.name: Utah
states.notes: Discharge: within 24 hours.

states.name: Vermont
states.notes: Discharge: within 72 hours. Quit: next payday or the following Friday — encoded as next_payday; FLAG: verify.
